name: Zoe Abbott

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m a senior researcher with the Work Futures Panel, an independent group. We have no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government; we sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. Tell me about a usual shift.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 43 and lead the evening booking and refund queue at our contact centre. I have a two-year college diploma, and I’m good at untangling a customer’s story when the booking and payment screens disagree. I earn at the higher end for this job. I use the approved AI summary now and then since another lead showed me a safe way to compare it with the original chat.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What part of that day stays with you after work?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My husband Mateo repairs heating systems, and our two children are in school. We have a mortgage and around ten months of expenses in savings. There are several contact centres within an easy journey, which gives us choices. I enjoy teaching an agent to find the missing payment; I do not enjoy measuring their work by how quickly they end a call.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AI Plateau is close to what I see now: a summary appears, and a person still has to find the refund. I would show the team where an original chat corrects an AI note.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my evening lead shift remains worth paying for. With ten months saved and several centres nearby, a quiet year leaves our mortgage secure.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep handling booking disputes and compare one AI summary a week with the original chat during the first year of this small change. I’d bring any mismatched refund amounts to our quality meeting.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm. I would rather spend one minute checking a note than make a customer call back three times.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which detail would you compare?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Last month the summary put the refund on the wrong card. The original chat had the last four digits, so I corrected the note before another agent acted.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What happens to the reserve?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would show Mateo (my husband) the same difference if he asked. We are keeping our ten-month savings for the mortgage and repairs, not spending it because the queue is quiet.

say: I’d tell agents to **check original chats** against AI refund summaries.
I’d raise **mismatched card amounts** at the quality meeting.
think: I think my **evening lead shift** remains useful in a mild change.
I trust our **ten-month savings** and nearby jobs to protect the mortgage.
do: Keep **handling booking disputes** and compare one AI summary weekly with original chats.
Bring **refund mismatches** to the centre’s quality meeting in the first year.
S0.quote: I would rather spend one minute checking a note than make a customer call back three times.
fieldNote: Her **AI use** is occasional and checked against original customer messages.
A **wrong card** in a summary gives her a concrete quality example.
She retains the **existing reserve** without promising new savings.

steps.text: Keep resolving booking disputes and check one AI summary against original chats weekly

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say Steady Disruption will take the straightforward booking replies first. I would ask managers to show how many paid evening shifts remain after the assistant starts answering them.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I can still teach agents the difficult refund cases, but there may be fewer agents and fewer paid lead hours. Our savings buy time to compare the nearby centres, not a permanent income.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d learn the new AI evidence screen with our quality lead by testing twenty old refund cases on a paid shift. In the first year routine replies move, I’d apply for a posted paid claims-review job only if its written weekly wage and hours cover our mortgage after travel and any childcare, and I would stay until a signed offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about a thinner rota, curious about the evidence screen. I can test a tool without promising it will keep my hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which old case would you test?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would include a case where the chatbot said a refund had been sent but the ledger showed only approval. The evidence screen should let us spot that before closing a ticket.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you count in a job offer?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Mateo (my husband) is on call some afternoons, so I would price care for those days. I would compare the whole week of pay after that cost, not the headline rate.

say: I’d request a **paid evening rota** after routine booking replies move.
I’d share **refund evidence errors** from a tested AI screen.
think: I think my **difficult-case teaching** could still be needed.
I fear **fewer paid lead hours** despite our savings.
do: Learn the **AI evidence screen** through twenty old cases on paid time in 2026.
Apply for **posted claims review** only with written after-cost mortgage-covering wages and hours; stay until signed offer.
feel: **Anxious** about the rota, curious about evidence.
S1.quote: I can test a tool without promising it will keep my hours.
fieldNote: Her **new AI learning** is a defined paid-shift test, not routine summary use.
She compares **whole-week wages** after travel and childcare.
The signed offer must precede leaving the **current paid role**.

steps.text: Learn AI evidence screen by testing twenty old refunds on a paid shift
Apply for posted claims review only with written after-cost mortgage-covering weekly wages/hours; leave after signing

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the team AGI by 2028 could answer refunds and judge them too. Robots around 2031 are not a delay for a screen queue, so we need staffing dates now.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my lead post might go even though I know the booking system well. Ten months saved and other centres nearby soften the first blow, but both children and the mortgage depend on a continuing wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d ask for written cut dates and examine posted paid appeals roles at the nearby centres. In the first year after 2028, if my hours end, I’d take a posted paid account-corrections role only after a signed offer with written weekly wages and hours covering the mortgage after travel and childcare; I would keep this job until then.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, with a plan I can check. A savings account is breathing room, not a new employer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What authority would a new role need?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask whether the new role lets me reverse a wrong refund or merely send another form. If it is only a handoff desk, I would keep looking.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the family compare?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Mateo (my husband) and I would lay the two rotas beside the children’s school times. His emergency calls can change a pickup with little notice, so the offer must leave a workable care plan.

say: I’d demand **written cut dates** for the evening queue.
I’d warn **2028 thinking AI** reaches refunds before robots.
think: I think my **lead post** could still disappear.
I see **ten months saved** as time to search, not lasting wages.
do: Request **written staffing dates** and inspect posted appeals roles in 2026.
Take **posted paid account-corrections work** after hours end only with signed written mortgage-covering wages/hours after travel and childcare, and workable care.
Require **refund reversal authority**; reject handoff-only roles and compare both rotas, school times and Mateo’s emergency-call care needs.
S2.quote: A savings account is breathing room, not a new employer.
fieldNote: Her **strong reserve** gives search time but does not replace wages.
She wants **refund correction authority** in any new role.
School pickup needs a **workable plan** around Mateo’s on-call shifts.

steps.text: Inspect posted appeals vacancies at nearby centres before 2028
Take corrections work after hours end only with signed written after-cost mortgage-covering pay/hours and workable care
Require authority to reverse wrong refunds; reject roles that only forward forms
Compare both work rotas with school times and Mateo’s on-call changes before agreeing care

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 gives us five years to see which paid appeals jobs are actually posted. I would ask other leads to join a request for correction authority and paid appeal shifts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I could move into training agents on disputes while people still handle calls. Yet full thinking AI may check those disputes too, so I need a real paid position rather than a course advert.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From 2026 I’d join leads in asking for paid appeals shifts and take a supervised paid trial teaching new agents only if the centre posts a paid trainer opening. If that job requires a training certificate, I’d take it only with employer-paid fees and paid study hours. In the first year after 2031, I’d move only on a signed offer with weekly wages and hours covering the mortgage after travel and school care.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy, but five years lets me try the work before giving up my queue. A paid trial tells me more than a glossy trainer title.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you teach on the trial?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would teach a trainee to follow one disputed refund from the chat to the ledger. If I could not give them paid time to practise, I would not call it a trainer post.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would the rota work at home?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask Mateo (my husband) to compare the trial rota and school pickup with his on-call days. We would not put both children into paid care for a role that barely covers the mortgage.

say: I’d ask other leads for **paid appeal shifts** and correction authority.
I’d support a **paid trainer trial** tied to a real vacancy.
think: I think I could teach **dispute work** to newer agents.
I know a **trainer title** is no shelter from 2031 AGI.
do: Join **leads’ appeals request**; try supervised paid trainer work only for a posted opening fitting pickup and Mateo’s on-call rota.
Take **required funded certificate** on paid study time only for that posted paid job.
Move after 2031 only with **signed after-cost mortgage-covering offer**, weekly hours and workable pickup.
feel: **Uneasy**, with time to test paid teaching.
S3.quote: A paid trial tells me more than a glossy trainer title.
fieldNote: The **trainer trial** must be paid and tied to a posted opening.
The certificate needs **funded study time** only if the posted role requires it.
Travel and care costs affect **whole-week net pay** before moving.

steps.text: Join leads requesting paid appeal shifts and correction authority
Try supervised paid trainer shift only for posted vacancy fitting pickup and Mateo’s on-call rota
Take posted trainer role’s required certificate only with employer-paid fees and paid study hours
Move after 2031 only on signed after-cost mortgage-covering wage, hours and pickup

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2036 gives our centre time to publish paid-hours forecasts instead of springing a new rota on families. I would ask the other leads to sign that request with me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I can keep earning well for several years, though full thinking AI could still take the booking queue in 2036. Robots around 2039 do not extend my desk deadline.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep leading evening refunds and join the leads’ written request for yearly paid-hours forecasts. In the first year after 2036, if my hours fall, I’d compare posted paid review jobs and take one only on a signed offer with written weekly wages and hours covering the mortgage after travel and childcare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about the far end, steady about this year. Ten months saved lets me say no to a job that breaks our week.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would leads request the forecast?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for the forecast by shift, because a full centre can still have no evening lead. The leads would all sign rather than each ask alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move the children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Mateo (my husband) and I would keep the children at their school. We would consider moving home only if a signed job offer covered the mortgage after new housing and travel costs and gave us a workable school journey.

say: I’d ask leads together for **yearly paid-hours forecasts** by shift.
I’d say **2036 thinking AI** reaches desks before robots.
think: I think I can **keep earning well** for several years.
I know **2036 AGI** may still end my booking queue.
do: Keep **leading refunds** and join a signed leads’ forecast request in 2026.
Take **posted review work** if hours fall only on signed after-cost mortgage-covering weekly wage and hours.
Consider **moving home** only on signed offer covering mortgage after housing and travel, with workable school journey.
S4.quote: Ten months saved lets me say no to a job that breaks our week.
fieldNote: Her **ten-month savings** buy choice without a new savings pledge.
The leads make a **shared worker demand** for shift-specific forecasts.
A family move needs **net mortgage-covering pay** and a workable school journey.

steps.text: Keep leading paid evening refund calls while they remain
Join other leads signing request for yearly paid-hours forecasts by shift
Take posted review job if hours fall only with signed written after-cost mortgage-covering weekly wages/hours
Consider moving home only with signed mortgage-covering offer after housing and travel, workable school journey

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 is the hardest, because our centre could remove both simple and hard booking work before staff know which paid posts remain. Ten months saved lets me investigate instead of grabbing the first opening. Written staffing dates, paid correction authority and a posted role with reliable whole-week pay would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask what a new rota does to the children’s afternoons. Mateo (my husband) sometimes takes emergency heating calls. A higher hourly rate can still cost us childcare when the new rota clashes with school pickup.

headlineQuote: A higher hourly rate can still cost us childcare when the new rota clashes with school pickup.
portrait: At **43**, Zoe is a highly skilled evening queue lead with a two-year diploma and higher pay.
She and Mateo have **two schoolchildren**, a mortgage and roughly ten months of expenses saved.
She uses **AI occasionally** for chat summaries and checks them against original messages.
Several nearby centres give her **real choices**, though school care and whole-week pay shape any move.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove both routine and difficult booking work before paid roles are clear.
whatWouldHelp: **Written staffing dates**, paid correction authority and reliable posted work would help.
